newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerians wept over hijacked Ethiopian plane crash.
newsitem.headline: Nigerians wept over hijacked Ethiopian plane crash.

text.p: Nigerians whose relatives were on the hijacked Ethiopian Airlines Boeing 767 which plunged into the sea near the Comoro Islands wept at Lagos airport when they were told of the fate of the plane.

The majority government-owned Sunday Times said the airlines office at the airport was shut and their officials were unavailable to give information to passengers who would have boarded the plane on the return flight from Lagos.
Many among the desperate crowd which thronged the airport on Saturday evening wept uncontrollably when the airport manager told them the plane had crashed, the paper said.

"God, I'm too young to be a widow," cried one middle-aged woman with her two children. The Sunday Times quoted her as saying that her husband, like some other Nigerians on the plane, was a vehicle spare parts trader.
A group of Indians was also at Lagos airport to find out if the plane had been to Bombay before the crash.

At least 67 out of the 175 passengers and crew were killed when the plane, flight ET 961, enroute from Addis Ababa to Abidjan, via Nairobi, Brazzaville and Lagos ran out of fuel after being hijacked and diverted towards the Comoran islands.
